name: Executive order of August 5, 1873 restoring part of the San Carlos division of the White Mountain reservation to the public domain
nations: Cibecue and Southern Tonto Apache groups (Western Apache, as named in Docket 22-D)
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It restored to the public domain the part of the San Carlos division of the White Mountain reservation (as set up by the order of December 14, 1872) lying east of and above the site of old Camp Goodwin (Royce p. 864, area 546).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission concluded that by the executive orders of August 5, 1873, July 21, 1874, April 27, 1876, January 26, 1877, March 31, 1877 and December 22, 1902 the United States successively extinguished, without paying compensation, Western Apache Indian title to lands inside the enlarged White Mountain reservation, as of the dates of the orders. The order of August 5, 1873 is one of the orders it named.

landTaken: Royce area 546: the part of the San Carlos division east of and above the site of old Camp Goodwin. The Commission did not reach the acreage because the claim was settled.
compensation: None at the time. The Western Apache claim (Docket 22-D) was compromised for $4,900,000 in 1972, for all the Western Apache lands taken.
today: The Fort Apache (White Mountain) and San Carlos reservations remain.

openQuestions: This tract (area 546) is not mapped on any other record, and the Commission names this order; it is counted as its own taking, as cession-1877-03-31-apache is for area 602. The Western Apache land outside the reservation is counted on cession-1886-10-01-apache-western-bands and the 1871 reserves on cession-1871-11-09-apache.
Whether all of area 546 lay inside the Western Apache title area of Finding 11 was not plotted; the Commission's per-tract acreage and value were never found because the claim was settled.
The order's own text was read only in Royce's summary.

Comm. 399) checked; Royce p. 864 (east of and above old Camp Goodwin) checked. The order is named in the Commission's taking holding, so it is broken under Jordan's 2026-11-08 rule. No change.

plain.promised: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It cut the land east of old Camp Goodwin out of the San Carlos part of the White Mountain reservation and opened it to settlers.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1969 that by this order and later ones the United States took Western Apache land inside the reservation without paying for it.
plain.today: The Western Apache claim was settled for $4,900,000 in 1972, for all their lands taken. The Fort Apache and San Carlos reservations remain.
